analyst_view.overall: Early view: second hosts fifth in a meeting of two of the league's three best defences (Lille 7 conceded, Lyon 9). Davide Ancelotti's Lille won 2-1 at Rennes before the break but host Bayern Munich four days later, while Lyon lost 2-0 at Brest and play Lillestrom in the Europa League on the Thursday after, so both may manage minutes.

goals.text: The numbers say 2.4 goals. I lean lower: Lille have kept five clean sheets and conceded only seven, Lyon have conceded nine, and both coaches have European games next. Lyon are also without Pavel Sulc (out until January) and may still be easing Lois Openda back from a leg injury.

corners.text: The numbers say 9.7 corners. I lean lower: Lille win only 3.6 corners a game (14th) and had two at Rennes, and Lyon average 4.6. Lyon did win eight at Brest with 69% of the ball, so the total depends on how much possession Lille concede.

cards.text: The numbers say 4.2 cards. That looks fair: Lille picked up three yellows at Rennes and Tanguy Nianzou was sent off against Lens earlier in the season, but Lyon are a low-foul side (11.6 a game). Nothing points strongly either way before the referee is known.

shots.text: The numbers say 21.9 shots. I stay close to it: season averages (Lille 11.4, Lyon 12.8) suggest a little more, but games between well-organised defences like these tend to be tight. Lille had only eight shots in their win at Rennes.

shots_on_target.text: The numbers say 8.3 shots on target. I lean lower: Lyon managed just two on target from 10 shots at Brest, Rennes managed two against Lille, and both defences protect the box well. Seven or so feels more likely.
